title: Samsung to use TSMC technology for Nvidia's next-generation memory chips, Seoul newspaper reports
gist: The Seoul Economic Daily reports Samsung will use TSMC's 3nm process for the base die of Nvidia's custom NVHBM, with Nvidia asking Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron to standardize on the same TSMC process. The report is sourced and not a formal joint announcement.

insights.claim: Samsung will reportedly adopt TSMC's three-nanometre process for the base die of Nvidia's custom high-bandwidth memory NVHBM, its first collaboration with TSMC at the HBM manufacturing stage.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Samsung's foundry rival becomes a supplier for a key HBM component.
insights.quote: The arrangement would mark Samsung’s first collaboration with the Taiwanese contract chipmaker at the HBM manufacturing stage

insights.claim: Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron to use the same TSMC process for NVHBM base dies and sixth-generation DRAM for core dies, to make suppliers' products perform consistently and reduce validation work.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Nvidia is using customer leverage to commoditize HBM suppliers and cut qualification effort.
insights.locator: Nvidia has asked its three memory suppliers

insights.claim: NVHBM, unveiled in August, puts Nvidia's custom memory controller into the base die beneath the stacked memory chips, which contains logic governing data transfers.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Moving controller logic into the base die shifts value toward Nvidia and the logic foundry.

insights.claim: Samsung intends to keep its integrated memory-core and base-die production for standard HBM and customised memory for others such as AMD, and is assessing whether its own foundry could make NVHBM base dies if demand exceeds TSMC capacity.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Samsung hedges by keeping its foundry as overflow capacity.

insights.claim: Customer requirements are reshaping semiconductor supply chain relationships, encouraging rivals to cooperate on selected components while competing elsewhere; the report rests on newspaper sources and is not a formal joint announcement.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Treat as unconfirmed reporting; coopetition driven by Nvidia demand is the structural theme.
insights.quote: the report should therefore be distinguished from a formal joint announcement
